upsc_summary: The Union Cabinet approved the extension of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme for five years (2026–27 to 2030–31) with a total outlay of Rs 3.15 lakh crore.
The central sector scheme provides income support of Rs 6,000 per year to eligible landholding farmer families in three equal instalments via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Since its launch in February 2019, over Rs 4.47 lakh crore has been disbursed across 23 instalments, with women farmers receiving over Rs 1.06 lakh crore (constituting ~25% of total beneficiaries).
According to NITI Aayog's DMEO evaluation, over 92% of beneficiaries utilized the funds for agricultural investments and 85% reported reduced dependence on informal credit.
Official data shows that during 2020–21 to 2025–26, area under cultivation increased by 9.65%, productivity by 10.53%, and total foodgrain production by 21.18%.

title: Monitoring of Essential Medicines in Hospitals
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI): Implemented under the National Health Mission (NHM) to reduce Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) by supporting States/UTs to provide free essential medicines in public health facilities.

Facility-wise Essential Medicines List (EML) norms: Recommended minimum essential drugs per tier — Sub Health Centre (SHC-AAM): 113; Primary Health Centre (PHC-AAM): 179; Community Health Centre (CHC): 301; Sub-District Hospital: 318; District Hospital (DH): 381.

Quality Assurance & IT Platforms: Quality ensured via mandatory Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) compliance and mandatory post-supply batch testing before distribution; monitored nationwide through the IT platform 'DVDMS' (Drugs & Vaccine Distribution Management System) and a Central Dashboard.

PMBJP Product Basket: Under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, basket covers 2,110 generic medicines and 315 surgicals/consumables, incorporating almost all generic items in the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM).

title: Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy Reforms
date: प्रविष्टि तिथि: 31 JUL 2026 2:28PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: DPCO 2013 Amendments: The Department of Pharmaceuticals notified key amendments to the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013 to enhance Ease of Doing Business and incentivize pharmaceutical R&D.

Elimination of Prior Price Approval: Once NPPA fixes the retail price of a new drug formulation for one manufacturer, subsequent manufacturers can adopt the same or lower price within 12 months without needing individual prior price approval.
Overcharging Liability Rationalization: Restricts a manufacturer's overcharging liability strictly to the stock quantity actually overcharged by individual distributors, retailers, or stockists.

Differentiated Pricing for Innovation: Permits fixing separate ceiling or retail prices for the same drug if justified by strong therapeutic rationale, encouraging innovations that improve patient health outcomes.
Reduced Compliance Burden: Record-keeping mandates for API sales, imports, and formulation packs are now capped at seven preceding financial years.
